newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX to launch Taiwan futures index on January 9.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX to launch Taiwan futures index on January 9.

text.p: The Singapore International Monetary Exchange (SIMEX) said on Thursday it would launch its Taiwan stock futures and options contracts on January 9, 1997.
The SIMEX's launch of the Taiwan contracts will come one day after the Chicago Mercantile Exchange's (CME) start of a Taiwan futures contract based on the Dow Jones Taiwan stock index.
The Singapore exchange said earlier this month it would begin its index in January, taking Taiwan's Securities and Exchange Commission by surprise.
SIMEX's launch intensifies pressure on Taiwan to speed up the start of its own futures exchange, which will be ready sometime in the third quarter next year.
The new SIMEX contracts will be based on the Taiwan stock index compiled by Morgan Stanley Capital International (MSCI).
The MSCI Taiwan Index is a market capitalisation-weighted index of 77 componenet stocks, representing a sampling of stocks covering 67 percent of the Taiwan stock market.
Each futures contract, which is cash settled and traded via an open outcry system, is US$100 multiplied by the MSCI Taiwan Index.

On the launch date, the opening bell for the first contract to be listed, the March 1997 contract, would be rung at 0055 GMT and trading would continue until the close of the market at 0415 GMT, the SIMEX said in a statement.
After the launch, trade hours would be from 0045 GMT to 0415 GMT, Monday to Friday, and 0045 GMT to 0315 GMT on Saturdays.
